summary: Wooden fire tower on White Oak Knob, Boone County, WV, added in the second half of 1937 to cover the Wharton area; listed as gone; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Listed as a former wooden tower; no source we read describes what, if anything, remains on the knob.

events.note: Added to the detection system in the second half of 1937, per a district ranger's report quoted in a February 1938 newspaper

evidence.supports: a new wooden fire tower added to the detection system in the period of the report
evidence.quote: One new wooden fire tower was added to the detection system during the period of this report.

evidence.supports: tower on White Oak Knob in Boone County; newspaper gives 2,000 feet
evidence.quote: It is located on White Oak knob in Boone county at an elevation of 2,000 feet.

evidence.supports: the report covered the second half of 1937
evidence.quote: From the 2nd half 1937 report by District Ranger.

evidence.supports: tower protected the Wharton area of Boone County
evidence.quote: This tower protected the Wharton area of Boone County.

evidence.supports: administered by the West Virginia Division of Forestry
register page carries a 1937 photograph courtesy of Jim Foster
state list describes the tower as wooden and gone
state number WV 26 is also listed for Sugar Grove

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1938 newspaper gives 2,000 feet; the register gives 1,856 ft (566 m). The record keeps the register figure of 566 m, and the story reports both.
The state number WV 26 is also listed for Sugar Grove (US 1678) on the state list; the register number US 1630 identifies this site.

sources.title: White Oak Knob Tower Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one dated 1930s item, and the state list is the only fate source. No staffing source found, so staffing is omitted. The register's 1937 photo (courtesy of Jim Foster) has no image URL in the text we read, so it is not in photos. Two WebSearch queries were run; no new White Oak sources surfaced. The brief's conflict note is explained: WV 26 is shared with Sugar Grove (US 1678). Wharton-area and Boone County newspapers were not searched and could fill the staffing and fate gaps.
